findings.statement: CA9 is the most strongly increased surface candidate in CPTAC: RNA is higher in tumours than in matched normal kidney [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.31], and the protein increase is confirmed [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.27].

The CA9 increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC paired tumour-normal RNA [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.71] and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=CA9; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=7.787], so it is tumour-cell signal rather than infiltration.

Single-cell data place CA9 in tumour cells: the RCC group holds most of its tumour transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=97.6%] and tumour cells exceed normal proximal tubule cells [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739].

In Visium sections the high-CA9 spots are explained by tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=spatial_expresser; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; composition_corrected_share=0.999] and their neighbours are enriched for tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381].

The CA9 AlphaFold model has moderate mean confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]; its top detected cavity has a descriptive structural-context score [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.546], and detected cavities recover part of the experimental ligand-contact residues [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. These describe a predicted monomer and do not identify a degron or predict degradation.
Open Targets lists antibody, PROTAC and small-molecule tractability for CA9 and the anti-CA9 antibody girentuximab at phase three, with a radiolabelled form at phase two.

Literature in the corpus reports CA9 as preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumour cells with low background in normal kidney, and CA9-targeted PET as proof-of-concept for noninvasive discrimination of ccRCC (PMID 42473996).

CA9 is not a dependency: its CRISPR effect in ccRCC lines is near zero [gene=CA9; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=0.051], so its value is as a homing antigen for conjugates or imaging, not as a gene the tumour needs.

CA9 is a known antibody-drug-conjugate or radioligand control with a high suitability score [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647], but Human Protein Atlas shows high staining in a vital organ, the stomach [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_staining_level=3.0], and in the weakest quarter of donors only a minority of tumour cells express it [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3].

CA9 is flagged as a PBRM1 subgroup candidate: TCGA RNA is higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148], and it is lower in ccB than ccA tumours [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-1.551].

In IMmotion150, higher CA9 expression is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib only as a non-significant trend [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336] with an adjusted p-value of [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.padj=0.332]; it does not separate the combination from sunitinib.

The tumour-cell attribution of CA9 holds in the second single-cell dataset (Zhang 2021), where tumour cells again hold most of its transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.981]; CA9 was not tested in the confirmatory CPTAC protein cohort because it is too sparse there.

CD70 is increased in tumours at RNA [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=4.46] and protein [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.42] level, replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=CD70; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=7.09] and remains increased at purity one [gene=CD70; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.278].
Open Targets lists clinical anti-CD70 agents, including cusatuzumab (phase two) and vorsetuzumab mafodotin (phase one).

Literature reports CD70 as commonly overexpressed in renal cell carcinoma with minimal normal-tissue expression and as a downstream hypoxia target (PMID 38195301), and describes new CD70-specific single-domain antibody radiotracers (PMID 39510586).

CD70 ranks among the top antibody-drug-conjugate candidates [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; rank=3] with a suitability score of [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746]; it is surface-annotated and not enriched in the vital-organ proteome, but Human Protein Atlas staining data are missing.

The cell attribution of CD70 is unstable between datasets: the tumour-cell share is low in Li 2022 [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.345] but high in Zhang 2021 [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.964], because T cells also express CD70.

CD70 is not a subgroup candidate: its differences between VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2 mutant and wild-type tumours are small and mostly non-significant across CPTAC RNA, CPTAC protein and TCGA, so it is a candidate across ccRCC rather than in one genetic subgroup.

In IMmotion150, higher CD70 is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.383], but not significantly, with an adjusted p-value of [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.166]; no gene separates the two arms.

SCARB1 tops the data-only target profile: tumour RNA [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=2.97] and protein [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.84] are increased, the change replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=SCARB1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=3.99] and grows at purity one [gene=SCARB1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.762].

UniProt places SCARB1 at the cell membrane and caveolae, and Open Targets gives it an association with ccRCC driven by genetics [gene=SCARB1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4049], but no clinical drug is listed.

Single-cell data show SCARB1 is not tumour-specific: endothelial cells express it most per cell, while tumour cells hold only part of its transcripts [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=33.6%] and macrophages a similar part.

SCARB1 protein is enriched in the adrenal gland in the GTEx normal proteome [gene=SCARB1; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.08], an on-target, off-tumour safety concern for any SCARB1-directed agent.

The SCARB1 protein increase replicates in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334] with an adjusted p-value of [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.28e-10].

NNMT protein is increased in tumours [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.71] and higher TCGA expression is associated with worse overall survival [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301].

Literature reports NNMT as upregulated in ccRCC tissue, with high expression correlating with worse survival, and calls it a promising prognostic biomarker and potential target (PMID 41399267); selective NNMT inhibitors have been described (PMID 37523719).

The NNMT protein increase replicates strongly in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776].

NNMT is tumour-cell intrinsic in both single-cell datasets: tumour cells hold most of its transcripts in Li 2022 [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.97] and in Zhang 2021 [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.948].

In the CheckMate trial of nivolumab versus everolimus, NNMT expression shows no association with outcome on nivolumab [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=0.083], with an adjusted p-value of [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.padj=0.88].

ENPP3 is increased at RNA [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=3.9] and protein [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.54] level and replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=ENPP3; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.56]; the antibody-drug conjugate AGS-16C3F reached phase two.

ENPP3 is a surface protein observed in the CSPA surfaceome with a conjugate suitability score of [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578], but it stains highly in normal kidney [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3.0] and in duodenum, which limits the therapeutic window.

SLC16A3 (MCT4) protein is increased in tumours [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.28] and the increase replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551], together with its measured phosphosite.
Literature links SLC16A3-mediated lactate export to M2 macrophage polarisation, suppressed CD8 T-cell function and immune evasion in ccRCC (PMID 42028950).

HK2 protein is increased in the discovery cohort [gene=HK2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.11] but does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256], which weakens it as a target.

The hexokinase inhibitor bromopyruvate is not selective for ccRCC lines in PRISM [gene=HK2; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; selectivity=-0.032], with an adjusted p-value of [gene=HK2; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; padj=0.862].

SCD is one of the few top target-profile genes with a CRISPR effect in ccRCC lines [gene=SCD; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=-0.501], but the effect is not selective versus other lines [gene=SCD; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=-0.078].

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) is the target of the approved drug belzutifan and has a strong Open Targets association with ccRCC [gene=EPAS1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4871].

Bulk omics underestimate EPAS1: protein is increased [gene=EPAS1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.16] while the RNA change is small [gene=EPAS1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=0.306]; in single-cell data endothelial cells express it in most cells [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=81.3%], so bulk EPAS1 mixes tumour and stromal signal.

EPAS1 shows the most ccRCC-selective CRISPR dependency among the checked targets [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], though it is not significant after correction [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; padj=0.061].

KDR (VEGFR2), target of approved drugs such as axitinib, cabozantinib and pazopanib, is an endothelial gene: endothelial cells hold most of its tumour transcripts [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=95.1%], so it is a microenvironment target, not a tumour-cell target.

In situ, high-KDR spots are explained by endothelium [gene=KDR; type=spatial_expresser; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=Endothelial; composition_corrected_share=0.99] and their neighbours are enriched for endothelial cells [gene=KDR; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=Endothelial; log2_enrichment=0.271].

KDR has one of the highest descriptive structural-context scores among candidates [gene=KDR; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.841], a monomer heuristic that does not identify a degron or ligase compatibility.

CD74 is an immune-cell gene: immune cells make nearly all its tumour transcripts [gene=CD74; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.972] and it tracks CD8 T-cell infiltration across tumours [gene=CD74; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_cd8_t_cells=0.684].

CXCR4 is expressed by infiltrating lymphocytes, with CD4 T cells expressing it in most cells [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD4_T; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=87.8%]; it is a microenvironment target.

The checkpoint control PDCD1 behaves as expected: immune cells make nearly all its transcripts [gene=PDCD1; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.998] and it correlates with CD8 T cells [gene=PDCD1; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_cd8_t_cells=0.811].

FCER1G, reported in the literature as abundant in ccRCC tissue and prognostic under nivolumab (PMID 35120484), is infiltration-driven: its RNA falls with tumour purity [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.692] and the tumour-normal change shrinks at purity one [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.061].

PSAT1 leads the biomarker profile: protein is decreased in tumours [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.96], the decrease replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=PSAT1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-2.974], and higher expression is associated with worse survival [gene=PSAT1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.43].

The PSAT1 protein decrease replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946].

Within tumours PSAT1 is higher in ccB than ccA tumours in TCGA [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=2.364] and higher in BAP1-mutant tumours [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711], consistent with its association with aggressive disease.

PCK1 is lost in tumours at protein level [gene=PCK1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.86], the loss replicates in TCGA [gene=PCK1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-3.079] and higher expression is associated with better survival [gene=PCK1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.415]: a marker of lost tubule identity.

ALDH6A1 is lost in tumours in TCGA [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-2.805] and is the strongest favourable prognostic gene among the biomarker leaders [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.554]; copy-number loss lowers its own RNA, a real dosage effect [gene=ALDH6A1; type=cis_dosage; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=14q; rna_rho=0.525].

VWF is increased in tumours [gene=VWF; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=3.599] and higher expression is associated with better survival [gene=VWF; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.397], reflecting the vascular component of ccRCC.

VHL is the dominant driver: it is mutated in nearly half of tumours [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483], its arm is lost in most CPTAC tumours [gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=0.791] and it has the top Open Targets association with ccRCC [gene=VHL; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6466].

PBRM1 is the second recurrent driver [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362], and loss of its copy lowers its own RNA [gene=PBRM1; type=cis_dosage; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; rna_rho=0.714] and protein [gene=PBRM1; type=cis_dosage; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; protein_rho=0.423], a real dosage effect of the arm loss that defines ccRCC.
SETD2 is a recurrent driver in a minority of tumours [gene=SETD2; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.119].
BAP1 is a recurrent driver in a minority of tumours [gene=BAP1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.104].

The most activated kinase after protein adjustment is RPS6KB1 (S6K1, downstream of mTOR) [gene=RPS6KB1; type=kinase_activity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PHOSPHOSITE; ksea_z=3.289] with an adjusted p-value of [gene=RPS6KB1; type=kinase_activity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PHOSPHOSITE; padj=0.038], consistent with the clinical use of mTOR inhibitors in ccRCC.

COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is the leading tumour-track discovery candidate: tumour cells hold most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], the increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.829] and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88].

COL23A1 has no clinical drug and is not prognostic in TCGA [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.123]; its conjugate suitability score is high [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.705], but staining data are missing, CSPA did not observe it at the cell surface, and in the weakest quarter of donors few tumour cells express it [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.5].

The COL23A1 AlphaFold model has low confidence [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91], so no reliable small-molecule cavity is available; antibody-based approaches fit better, and dependency or functional evidence is still missing.

RAB42, a small GTPase with very few ccRCC papers, is the second tumour-track candidate: tumour cells hold most of its transcripts [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627], it replicates in TCGA [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.371] and is purity-robust [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189]; its surface location is not established, so antibody access is uncertain, and no selective dependency is seen.

OLFML2A, a secreted fibroblast protein seen in the CSPA surfaceome, is a leading stroma-track candidate: fibroblasts hold most of its tumour transcripts [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647], the increase replicates in TCGA [gene=OLFML2A; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=2.372] and survives at purity one [gene=OLFML2A; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.527].

COX4I2 is a stroma-track candidate made mainly by fibroblasts [gene=COX4I2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.893] that replicates in TCGA [gene=COX4I2; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=2.139]; it is an internal mitochondrial subunit, so it is not antibody-accessible.

MILR1 tops the immune track (a macrophage gene with no ccRCC papers), but it is infiltration-driven: the TCGA increase [gene=MILR1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=2.436] nearly vanishes at purity one [gene=MILR1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414], and higher expression is associated with worse survival [gene=MILR1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.343].

LILRB4, a macrophage inhibitory receptor, is almost entirely immune-made [gene=LILRB4; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] and tracks the immune score [gene=LILRB4; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.853]; its bulk increase shrinks at purity one [gene=LILRB4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.508], so it marks hot tumours rather than tumour cells.

caveats: All values come from CPTAC discovery, TCGA-KIRC and public single-cell, spatial and trial datasets; associations are not causal and no candidate was tested functionally here.
No leading candidate of the target profile is a selective DepMap dependency; two-dimensional cell lines also miss HIF-2 biology.
Structural-context scores describe predicted monomers and do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or degradation.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; literature novelty is counted by gene symbol and can miss aliases.
Trial associations come from single arms of under one hundred patients and no gene separates trial arms after correction.
The literature corpus is a few hundred ccRCC abstracts; absence of literature here does not mean absence in PubMed.
The convergence_ranking call for the overall profile timed out in this session; the overall ranking was read from convergence.json instead.
